title: F-22 fidelity implementation plan

priority_definitions.P0: Resolve configuration/evidence/dependency decisions before dependent implementation.
priority_definitions.P1: First implementation tranche: documented functional omissions or a concrete user-path/physical inconsistency.
priority_definitions.P2: Follow-on depth and coherent normal/limit/degraded behavior.
priority_definitions.P3: Optional/interface/analogue policy choice; not automatically a required F-22 fix.

work_packages.title: Freeze the aircraft and evidence baseline
work_packages.change: Choose a dated F-22 configuration and equipment list. Record each supported real behavior, adopted analogue and unresolved parameter before writing fixes. Preserve explicit alternatives when sources conflict.
work_packages.gate: A configuration sheet identifies era/software/equipment, land-based recovery, optional equipment exclusions and adopted substitutes. No modern requirement is silently treated as fleet-wide fielding.

work_packages.title: Correct the physical model and define performance envelopes
work_packages.change: Resolve the CG/force-point dependency, identify any host ground-effect contribution and add the missing owned contribution where needed; then calibrate thrust, drag, fuel and approach behavior under matched conditions. Keep public capability anchors separate from unknown production curves.
work_packages.gate: An envelope matrix records mass, CG, stores/doors, pressure altitude, temperature, wind and engine setting for steady climb/cruise, acceleration, turn, approach and ground-roll cases. Source-limited parameters remain estimates with stated bounds.

work_packages.title: Make power, starting, hydraulics and emergency sources coherent
work_packages.change: Define consumer supply and surviving-source topology; add the documented SES/APU/emergency gear functions, then resource recovery, compartment isolation and hook function. Do not copy Hornet start/gear hardware over known F-22 evidence.
work_packages.gate: Normal, single-source-loss, dual-source-loss and exhausted-reserve scenarios have consistent achieved consumer states. Restoration never creates energy or replays a stale command.

work_packages.title: Connect fuel, oxygen, cabin and cooling dependencies
work_packages.change: Separate stored fuel from feed availability, preserve finite start/APU combustion accounting, and connect engine bleed, cabin/OBOGS and supported backup. Define thermal/fault indications only within available references.
work_packages.gate: Stored-versus-feed quantity, mass debit and warning state agree through depletion, supply loss and recovery. Estimated rates/thresholds are not presented as F-22 operating limits.

work_packages.title: Build a coherent navigation and approach instrument chain
work_packages.change: Provide independent navigation-source/reversion behavior, valid LOC/GS/TACAN components, coherent barometric/radar altitude and defined landing-cue geometry. Calibrate the E-bracket against the aerodynamic model rather than transplanting another aircraft AoA.
work_packages.gate: A land-based recovery matrix covers manual visual/ILS/TACAN/overhead where adopted, missed approach/go-around, component loss, touchdown, braking and refueling-state indications. CASE I/II/III and carrier ACLS remain comparator procedures unless deliberately added as optional equipment.

work_packages.title: Resolve AFCS engagement, override and recovery interactions
work_packages.change: Use one explicit AFCS substitute interaction policy, decide and label ordinary-paddle versus dedicated-override behavior per mode, and correct altitude/heading request paths. Then complete guidance, degraded disengagement and ATC if adopted. Separate advisory terrain escape from any supported automatic recovery.
work_packages.gate: Pilot selection, engagement gates, axis ownership, temporary override, permanent disconnect, recapture and power/fault recovery agree in both cockpit and flight response. Optional autoland/automatic collision recovery requires a separately justified baseline.

work_packages.title: Give radar tasking observable AESA depth
work_packages.change: Define an observable game task-service model with explicit coverage, track priority, revisit/age, saturation and reduced-array states. Align focus and native sensing; keep rendering, detection and estimate updates separate.
work_packages.gate: Controlled task-load/coverage cases show the declared service tradeoffs. Silence stops new own-radar measurements; powered passive receivers and donor sources continue and age their own observations. No invented APG-77 range, waveform, LPI invisibility or scheduler is claimed.

work_packages.title: Preserve evidence through identification, fusion and networks
work_packages.change: Keep observation time, receipt time, donor/source, identity conflict and pilot declaration distinct. Build independent freshness for each source/field and, if adopted, planned-intelligence behavior before expanding display convenience.
work_packages.gate: Conflicting, late, duplicate, stale and lost-source observations never become unwarranted hostile certainty or a fresh own-sensor measurement.

work_packages.title: Complete warning and countermeasure program semantics
work_packages.change: Manual program work can proceed independently; WP07 is a dependency only for later threat-input integration into SEMI/AUTO. Adopt the existing flat Hornet-like scheme coherently, or explicitly choose a nested alternative. Separate edit/display bank from execution bank; add declared draft/save, mode/consent, interruption, inventory and readiness rules.
work_packages.gate: Generic inert timing/inventory scenarios establish selection/execution, bounds, partial exhaustion, power interruption and restore without any threat-specific recipes, effectiveness assumptions or automatic defensive optimization.

work_packages.title: Tie stores programming and consent to achieved weapon state
work_packages.change: Separate sensor cue, actual seeker acquisition, readiness, mission initialization, programming, release conditions, actual release and inventory. Keep training and jettison distinct.
work_packages.gate: A declared supported-store set has normal, rejected, stale, inhibited, power-loss and acknowledgement cases with achieved status. Unsupported TGP/HMD/HARM/Maverick/naval weapons are equipment decisions, not automatic F-22 defects.

work_packages.title: Finish CNI, display transactions and presentation
work_packages.change: Integrate the owned radio workflow, truthful achieved readback and surviving CNI functions. Retain coherent display layouts, held-command release and brightness/fault separation; add optional map/checklist/planned-intelligence depth only under the adopted policy.
work_packages.gate: Tuning, receive/audio, focused controls, numeric commit/cancel, display relocation, lighting and surviving CNI all follow their stated contracts across failures and restoration.

work_packages.title: Validate integrated alert lifecycle and coupled failure recovery
work_packages.change: Give each supported equipment condition its own validity, occurrence and acknowledgement state. Keep terrain/navigation gates, audio suppression, master attention and downstream utility supply states distinct. Optional general cockpit-design ideas remain adoption choices.
work_packages.gate: Fault A acknowledged plus new fault B re-alerts as adopted; independent faults survive unrelated sensor loss; clearing a detected temperature does not falsely restore an isolated supply. Synthetic probes and runtime observations retain separate evidence scopes.

work_packages.title: Close findings with evidence and keep the guide current
work_packages.change: Implement in bounded changes tied to finding IDs. Attach the new code revision, normal/limit/degraded observations and reference version to each closure; update dependencies and assumptions when a correction changes the target.
work_packages.gate: Closure requires evidence for the stated behavior, not merely a passing callback/test or a matching label. A fully tested estimate remains an estimate; new primary evidence can reopen it.

findings.behavior: Integrated pitch-only thrust vectoring and physical travel
findings.applicability: Production engine capability; no claim that ±20 degrees is available at every flight condition.
findings.change: Retain integrated pitch vectoring with an absolute ±20-degree mechanical bound. Label the mod’s Mach, gear and hydraulic schedules as estimates rather than asserting that the brochure authenticates them.
normal_cases: At a supported low-Mach condition, compare command, achieved left/right angle and force direction.
limit_cases: Sweep each mechanical bound and the estimated Mach/gear schedules.
failure_recovery_cases: Remove one hydraulic supply; retain independent achieved nozzle states and opposite-engine behavior.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: APU supplies aircraft ground utilities with engines stopped
findings.applicability: F-22 ground-maintenance capability; exact bus ratings and permissible ground procedures are not supplied.
findings.change: Route a running APU to the supported limited ground electrical, hydraulic and conditioned-air consumers. Keep ratings, consumer priorities and pneumatic conditioning as explicit estimates where not documented; do not treat the APU readiness lamp as proof of all three supplies.
normal_cases: With engines/cart off, verify the declared APU ground electrical, hydraulic and conditioned-air consumers separately.
limit_cases: Keep limited consumer capacity and conditioning requirements explicit; one ready indication does not certify all outputs.
failure_recovery_cases: Stop/fault APU, then restore a qualified source; all dependent physical supplies and indications follow the declared handoff.

findings.behavior: Four pressure-compensated engine-driven pumps
findings.applicability: Supplier hardware specification, April 2014; total flow ratings do not establish simultaneous full flow at all conditions.
findings.change: Represent four pumps feeding the intended circuits sufficiently to preserve single-pump redundancy and reduced available flow. Keep pump outlet rating, regulated pressure and displayed consumer pressure distinct; do not declare 3,950 wrong without identifying its measurement point.
normal_cases: Document pump-to-circuit abstraction and steady pressure/flow at one and two engines.
limit_cases: Exercise concurrent demand against reduced source capacity without assuming the sum of rated flows is always available.
failure_recovery_cases: Compare individual pump loss with full circuit loss and recovery.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Utility normal supply is distinguished from maintenance transfer
findings.applicability: Documented maintenance switching function only; not a complete circuit schematic or authenticated left/right mapping.
findings.change: Identify the actual utility consumers and mapping before changing failed-side behavior. Represent the documented normal/maintenance transfer distinction where applicable. Preserve independent flight-control redundancy; do not use this brochure alone to forbid every automatic backup path.
normal_cases: Identify the actual consumers controlled by the documented utility selector and their normal source.
limit_cases: Compare maintenance transfer with ordinary operation after circuit mapping is established.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose a normal source and check only documented or explicitly estimated backup behavior.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Rudder retains supply from either hydraulic system
findings.applicability: Functional comparison of the documented shuttle; no authenticated transient data.
findings.change: Retain the functional ability to power the rudder from either independent side, preserving physical supply isolation and any documented switching delay if later found. Do not require detailed valve geometry merely to count the hardware.
normal_cases: Command rudder with both hydraulic supplies healthy.
limit_cases: Limit one supply while retaining the other; compare achieved rudder motion.
failure_recovery_cases: Fail either side independently, then both; restore one side without healing physical damage.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: APU-driven emergency hydraulic source
findings.applicability: Documented emergency source capability; no inferred automatic-start or airborne envelope.
findings.change: Provide an APU hydraulic source with lower available flow than the main pumps. Keep emergency activation criteria, flight envelope and consumer priorities explicitly unresolved; the rating does not disclose them.
normal_cases: With engines off, make the APU hydraulic source available to documented supported consumers.
limit_cases: Constrain modeled flow separately from source pressure.
failure_recovery_cases: Remove APU source while main pumps are absent, then recover a main source.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Main gear door/strut hydraulic sequencing
findings.applicability: Supplier-documented main-gear sequencing; absence of independent EFM door states is not proof of incorrect visible sequencing.
findings.change: Use the documented mechanically ordered door/strut relationship as the target and inspect the existing EDM phases before changing the normal sequence. Preserve that order under pressure interruption; exact timings/angles remain estimated.
normal_cases: Inspect existing EDM phases during a full normal main-gear cycle before replacing animation.
limit_cases: Interrupt at each door/strut phase and resume preserving the selected order.
failure_recovery_cases: Remove pressure or jam one leg; reported safe/unsafe state follows achieved locks.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Pressure-maintained hydraulic fuel boost
findings.applicability: Documented normal feed mechanism, without complete emergency/gravity-flow schematic.
findings.change: Distinguish tank quantity from pressure-qualified engine feed and represent hydraulic boost availability. Do not invent exact starvation delay or alternate/gravity-feed capability from the component description.
normal_cases: Transfer stored fuel through the modeled boost/feed path during steady engine use.
limit_cases: Maintain total quantity while limiting transfer or boost source.
failure_recovery_cases: Fail/recover boost supply; use only documented or declared estimated alternate feed rather than immediate arbitrary starvation.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Wheel-slip and navigation-deceleration brake control
findings.applicability: Documented functional behavior; no real pedal schedule, gains, friction chart or stop-distance performance is inferred.
findings.change: Establish native DCS braking semantics, then adopt wheel-slip/navigation feedback and a declared pedal-to-deceleration relationship appropriate to the selected aircraft profile. Do not recreate the early EMD threshold/heat defect or assume an anti-skid enable flag proves the complete controller.
normal_cases: Measure pedal demand, wheel speed, ground speed and deceleration on a declared dry runway.
limit_cases: Repeat low-friction, asymmetric braking and delayed spin-up with controlled mass/speed.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose a reference or supply and identify native versus owned degraded braking.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: OBOGS depends on engine bleed and cabin environment
findings.applicability: Primary-source function; detailed 2012 hardware deficiencies are not automatically applicable to a modern configured aircraft.
findings.change: Separate conditioned-source availability, delivered pressure, oxygen-product availability/concentration and cabin pressure in the declared simplified model. Publish the correct SDK pressure quantity; use source/cabin dependence and era-appropriate backup without importing old warning delays, obsolete deficiencies or a clinical onset curve.
normal_cases: Track source availability, oxygen-product state, exported pressure and cabin pressure as separately named quantities.
limit_cases: Vary cabin/source state without treating 101000 Pa as an oxygen percentage or assuming its unspecified pressure-reference convention.
failure_recovery_cases: Interrupt and restore primary source; the declared backup and host interface follow the actual selected source, without a guessed clinical onset timeline.

findings.behavior: Automatic backup oxygen after primary interruption
findings.applicability: Use the selected aircraft era: the pre-ABOS manual EOS account and post-modification automatic backup are not interchangeable. Current ABOS capacity, trigger/reversion details and host pilot effects remain unresolved.
findings.change: For a declared ABOS-equipped profile, provide automatic finite backup after primary interruption. Keep its reserve and transfer/reversion assumptions explicit; do not substitute the older manual-only action or its endurance range for modern ABOS data.
normal_cases: For the selected ABOS-era profile, interrupt primary supply and verify automatic backup rather than requiring the pre-ABOS manual-only action.
limit_cases: Use finite declared reserve and separately identify modern ABOS unknowns; do not import the original EOS endurance range.
failure_recovery_cases: Restore primary supply or exhaust backup according to labeled transfer/reversion assumptions; no invisible reserve replenishment.

findings.behavior: Published internal fuel capacity
findings.applicability: Aggregate capacity only; rounded imperial/metric figures are not exact simultaneous specifications.
findings.change: Keep 8,200 kg as the documented rounded capacity baseline; separately model usable feed and operating reserves without silently increasing the published internal total.
normal_cases: Fill internal fuel to the rounded published capacity.
limit_cases: Bound partial/maximum fill and keep external capacity separate.
failure_recovery_cases: Repair/rearm must not silently create internal fuel outside the selected service.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Supersonic flight without afterburner
findings.applicability: Capability comparison, not a demand to copy another fighter’s thrust or a classified installed engine deck.
findings.change: Use sustained supersonic dry-power capability as the public target. Leave exact Mach/altitude/mass claims unresolved until measured against a publicly defensible condition.
normal_cases: Use PF02 matched-condition sustained dry-power assessment.
limit_cases: Separate steady speed from a coast following AB/descent.
failure_recovery_cases: Evaluate degraded propulsion separately, without requiring one-engine supercruise.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Automatic shutdown after second generator
findings.applicability: Automatic shutdown rule is an analogue; do not transfer Hornet APU supply topology to F-22.
findings.change: If using Hornet behavior as the explicit fallback, require both generators continuously online for 60 seconds. Mark that timing/criterion as a chosen analogue until an F-22-specific rule is found.
normal_cases: Under the selected Hornet analogue, qualify the timer after both generators online.
limit_cases: Interrupt the condition just before the full minute; qualification must restart.
failure_recovery_cases: Keep one generator failed with both engines at idle and compare with the declared F-22 estimate.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: APU starting draws on the F-22 Stored Energy System
findings.applicability: Historical 2006 F-22 architecture; current configuration and operating limits require corroboration.
findings.change: Represent a bounded SES air/fuel start reserve and the APU start/door demands at simulation depth. Keep charge pressures, quantities, refill rate and permitted attempts as explicit estimates; do not derive them from the inconsistent rescue quantity tables.
normal_cases: A charged estimated SES permits APU start and the declared door operation.
limit_cases: Repeated/aborted starts use finite air/fuel without importing Hornet accumulator quantities.
failure_recovery_cases: Deplete one SES source, restore it through the declared service/charge path and retry.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Pilot separates cranking from fuel introduction
findings.applicability: Both source procedures are DCS comparators; a genuinely automated F119 start could differ legitimately.
findings.change: Establish the intended F-22 start-control assumption before changing the pilot workflow. Keep the current automatic sequence if selected, but make source energy, fuel introduction, lightoff and abort physically coherent. Offer the exact two-stage comparator only as a labeled alternative.
normal_cases: Document and execute the selected automated or two-stage start sequence.
limit_cases: Abort before and after lightoff; separate dry cranking from combustion.
failure_recovery_cases: Remove starter energy, ignition or usable fuel and show a coherent failed-start outcome.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Windmilling / cross-bleed relight depends on flight condition and a surviving source
findings.applicability: Dual-engine Hornet analogy; comparator limits describe that DCS aircraft only.
findings.change: Use distinct windmilling and source-assisted restart behavior as the fallback. Declare conservative estimated F119 limits separately rather than asserting the Hornet’s exact envelope is F-22 data.
normal_cases: A stopped engine and a naturally windmilling engine produce distinct rotor indications.
limit_cases: Vary airflow/altitude under labeled estimated F119 restart bounds; do not use Hornet numbers as F-22 limits.
failure_recovery_cases: Compare unassisted and source-assisted relight with unavailable/damaged sources.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Main RPM indication represents compressor/core speed
findings.applicability: Semantic match to selected DCS analogue, not validation of F119 spool dynamics or absolute shaft RPM anchors.
findings.change: Keep core-percent RPM explicitly distinguished from fan speed. Do not relabel fan percent or arbitrary raw RPM as the engine’s main cockpit RPM.
normal_cases: Compare core/fan states with each separately labeled indication.
limit_cases: Sweep transients where fan and core lag differ.
failure_recovery_cases: Loss/invalid data must not silently relabel fan speed as core.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Displayed fuel flow: main burner versus total augmentation flow
findings.applicability: This difference alone is not a demonstrated F-22 error; F-22 flow semantics need their own source.
findings.change: Explicitly choose and label main-burner or total-flow semantics. If choosing Hornet as fallback, separate main and augmentor consumption and display only main flow; aircraft mass must still account for both.
normal_cases: Select and label total-flow or main-burner-only indication while accounting for all mass loss.
limit_cases: Compare idle/dry/AB transitions and units.
failure_recovery_cases: An unlit augmentor with scheduled/preflow fuel follows the declared failure policy.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: External tanks need pressure and selectable transfer states
findings.applicability: External-tank behavior is an analogue, not a claim the F-22 has a Hornet probe or centerline tank.
findings.change: Use a declared external-transfer profile with pressure/selection consequences and independent tank quantities. Choose one analogy coherently; do not combine incompatible Hornet and Viper control schemes.
normal_cases: Apply one declared external transfer/pressure policy and observe independent station quantities.
limit_cases: Exercise ground/refueling/empty/asymmetric tank states without blending incompatible controls.
failure_recovery_cases: Remove a transfer source or tank and recover without replenishing fuel invisibly.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Separate feed cells, transfer cells and tank pressurization
findings.applicability: Historical F-22 architecture; source fuel quantities are not adopted.
findings.change: Use a small automatic feed/transfer model preserving a distinction between fuel stored elsewhere and fuel available to the engine, plus a bounded pressurization availability state. Keep geometry, transfer rates, balance priorities and degraded-feed endurance estimated. Do not invent a Viper-style F-22 cockpit selector.
normal_cases: Automatic transfer maintains feed availability from the declared separate cell abstraction.
limit_cases: Use fuel elsewhere while a feed cell is low; track balance separately from aggregate quantity.
failure_recovery_cases: Fail a transfer path or pressurization availability and recover using labeled estimates.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Pilot-set bingo and associated caution/audio
findings.applicability: Comparator behavior; inherited draw-argument logic is not established as a complete usable equivalent.
findings.change: Provide a pilot-editable bingo quantity and a threshold crossing with caution/audio, adapting entry to the F-22 ICP rather than copying an IFEI bezel. Keep bingo separate from automatic feed-low.
normal_cases: Enter a bingo threshold through an F-22-appropriate interface and cross it once.
limit_cases: Adjust threshold above/below current quantity with declared alert persistence.
failure_recovery_cases: Power-cycle or refuel through the threshold without a stale or permanently latched alert.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Feed-tank low warning distinct from total/bingo
findings.applicability: Comparison of warning function; numeric F-22 threshold unresolved.
findings.change: Create a separate availability warning from the selected feed-reservoir abstraction, with declared persistence/hysteresis. Use the Hornet 800-lb/1-minute rule only if explicitly choosing that complete analogue; do not claim it as an F-22 limit.
normal_cases: Distinguish total/bingo quantity from a feed availability warning.
limit_cases: Cross low-feed threshold with fuel still in transfer cells and apply declared persistence.
failure_recovery_cases: Restore transfer/feed and clear warning according to a distinct recovery condition.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Parking brake auto-release with power advance
findings.applicability: F-16-specific chosen fallback; Hornet parking mechanism differs and should not be mixed into the same claim.
findings.change: If selecting the Viper workflow as the fallback, release the actual parking state and switch indication with power advance as well as manual release. Resolve the 80-versus-85-percent source inconsistency before claiming an exact threshold; an estimated threshold must be labeled.
normal_cases: Set parking brake and manually release the actual latch/switch state.
limit_cases: Advance power through the selected estimated release condition, resolving the source threshold conflict.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose hydraulic reserve and distinguish selected PARK from supported holding force.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Pilot engages steering and receives steering status
findings.applicability: DCS Viper operational control analogy, not proof of an F-22 NWS switch or exact limits.
findings.change: Use an explicitly chosen armed/engaged steering control and honest status. Retain estimated F-22 angles separately; the Viper source justifies the workflow, not the mod’s60/25-degree schedule.
normal_cases: Arm/engage the chosen steering state and compare pilot status with wheel motion.
limit_cases: Cross the estimated speed boundaries with fixed pedal and nosewheel unloading.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose/recover power or nose contact; steering status follows actual availability.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Emergency extension has a Stored Energy System air source
findings.applicability: Historical F-22 energy path; detailed operational limits are unavailable.
findings.change: Represent an explicitly bounded SES-powered emergency extension with independent deployed/locked result and depletion. Keep the production cockpit action, detailed door sequence, pressures and timings unresolved or labeled estimates; do not invent a Hornet handle.
normal_cases: Use the declared alternate action to extend gear with normal hydraulic sources unavailable.
limit_cases: Share finite SES energy with its other supported consumers and identify insufficient reserve.
failure_recovery_cases: Interrupt normal cycle, command alternate extension and verify the achieved lock/unsafe result.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Flap selection schedules achieved surfaces and flight law
findings.applicability: Physical scheduling comparison; Hornet naval flap angles are not prescribed for F-22.
findings.change: Use the documented historical F-22 configuration distinction if the declared profile adopts it; coordinate flap, roll and on-speed state as in VG05. Estimate the remaining schedule explicitly and keep Hornet scheduling only as a named fallback; do not invent HALF/FULL F-22 panel controls.
normal_cases: Transition through declared takeoff/cruise/approach/refuel surface schedules.
limit_cases: Cross estimated speed/configuration boundaries and compare achieved surfaces with forces.
failure_recovery_cases: Fail a surface/source or return from manual override without a discontinuous law handoff.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Trim-inhibit versus autopilot disconnect
findings.applicability: Specific DCS Viper control behavior; mod trim rates remain estimates, not judged wrong solely for being undocumented.
findings.change: If adopting this fallback safety function, define an explicit trim-inhibited state with matching indication while keeping AP and trim permissions distinct. Do not add a real-F-22 label without evidence.
normal_cases: Keep trim inhibit distinct from AP disconnect in the chosen analogue policy.
limit_cases: Hold trim across the inhibit boundary and verify no hidden motion/indicator drift.
failure_recovery_cases: Restore trim permission; a stale held command follows an explicitly selected recovery policy.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Resettable FCS faults versus persistent mechanical damage
findings.applicability: System fault/test behavior is the comparison; host repair callback and arbitrary total-destruction policy are outside real-aircraft authenticity scoring.
findings.change: Add a limited documented-analogue reset/test workflow with in-test/pass/active-fault outcomes; do not let a cockpit reset heal damaged hardware. Do not grade the mod’s arbitrary destruction threshold as authentic or inauthentic without a reference.
normal_cases: Run the chosen FCS reset/test workflow through IN TEST and pass/fail outcomes.
limit_cases: Reset a transient condition without making active physical damage disappear.
failure_recovery_cases: Persistent damage remains failed after reset/BIT until physical repair.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Oil warning delay and recovery hysteresis
findings.applicability: F110-equipped DCS Viper warning comparison; exact F119 pressure is not inferred.
findings.change: Choose one coherent engine-lubrication analogue for the pressure curve and alert timing; retain F119 numbers as unknown. Use delayed low-pressure detection and a distinct recovery threshold as explicit simulation assumptions rather than mixing F110 thresholds into an unrelated estimated curve.
normal_cases: Use one coherent declared oil scale and low-pressure detection policy.
limit_cases: Cross low and recovery thresholds, including short dips below the delay.
failure_recovery_cases: Recover a pressure fault and distinguish warning recovery from physical repair.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Low-voltage battery supply coexists with high-voltage ground input
findings.applicability: Narrow documented voltage-domain comparison, not certification of the full current bus distribution.
findings.change: Retain an identified 28 V battery/charger domain and document the 270 V ground input separately. Keep the discharge curve, capacity and conversion behavior as estimates; add conversion/source failures only where they change a supported consumer behavior.
normal_cases: Identify battery/charger nominal 28 V separately from the 270 V external interface.
limit_cases: Document estimated capacity/discharge behavior without claiming an authentic battery curve.
failure_recovery_cases: A source/conversion fault affects only consumers assigned to that modeled domain.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Fire selection isolates a compartment before separate discharge
findings.applicability: Historical rescue-function comparison; not a current operational checklist.
findings.change: Implement compartment detection/selection, isolation and finite discharge as distinct simulator states with the documented functional ordering. Leave bottle count, agent quantity, detection thresholds and current messages as estimates or unknown. Do not let a fire-test indication create a fire.
normal_cases: Select the affected compartment, observe isolation and then distinct finite discharge.
limit_cases: Test indication without producing a real fire; READY and DISCH reflect different states.
failure_recovery_cases: Fail detection or suppress without successful extinction; prohibit source restoration while selected isolation remains.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Commanded pneumatic arresting-gear extension and retraction
findings.applicability: Historical land-based recovery hardware; host arrestment support is unresolved.
findings.change: Add a commanded, achieved pneumatic hook state with available source and a defined DCS runway-arrestment interaction. Keep exact cockpit controls, travel/timing and allowed loads estimated. Do not copy carrier recovery modes into a land-based F-22 profile.
normal_cases: Command and retract the achieved hook with available estimated pneumatic supply.
limit_cases: Verify host cable/contact support separately from animation.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose source or jam hook and retain an honest requested-versus-achieved state.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Brake heat persists and can increase after stopping
findings.applicability: Physical persistence target only; historical rescue waiting periods are not a calibration curve.
findings.change: Establish host thermal/tire behavior first. If absent, add a bounded brake-energy and heat-soak abstraction that persists after stopping, with estimated cooling and consequences explicitly labeled. Avoid treating hydraulic reserve as thermal energy.
normal_cases: Identify host thermal behavior or compute brake energy from actual braking work.
limit_cases: Compare one stop with repeated braking and post-stop heat redistribution.
failure_recovery_cases: Cool/refill/repair according to declared physical service; hydraulic pressure recovery does not instantly remove heat.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; this audit did not change aircraft implementation.

findings.behavior: Combustion and auxiliary power draw finite fuel

findings.requirement_kind: proposed substitute or coherent game-state contract; exact F-22 procedure unresolved
findings.status: open; audit does not modify aircraft implementation
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Airspeed limit attention cue versus structural/dynamic limits
findings.applicability: Historical EMD function supports the role; current production thresholds and host-native contribution remain unverified.
findings.change: For the selected profile, expose an airspeed-limit state with a declared provisional CAS/Mach/configuration envelope and hysteresis. Keep warning, aerodynamic response and actual damage distinct. Production F-22 trigger values, exact words and lead time remain unresolved.
normal_cases: In an adopted clean configuration, enter/leave a declared provisional speed-attention region and get one coherent indication.
limit_cases: CAS and Mach limits are evaluated separately; ground/gear/store configuration changes do not silently use an unrelated clean limit.
failure_recovery_cases: Invalid airspeed is indicated as unavailable instead of either a valid overspeed or an all-clear; restore without a false crossing.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Equipment alert validity is distinct from navigation/terrain validity
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: Split power and validity gates by alert family. Terrain prediction needs geometric validity; a valid equipment failure should use its own source validity and phase policy. Declare normal-start inhibits separately instead of treating all ground faults as irrelevant.
normal_cases: A valid independent equipment fault is available with required alerting power on the ground where the adopted policy calls for it.
limit_cases: Remove HUD/navigation validity while preserving a valid equipment-fault source; only dependent alerts become unavailable.
failure_recovery_cases: Restore navigation without erasing, replaying or falsely acknowledging the independent fault.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Master attention acknowledgement is separate from fixing a fault
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: Represent active fault, new attention demand, pilot acknowledgement and physical recovery separately. Apply the chosen acknowledge action to the appropriate master attention while retaining the underlying active condition and any noncancellable urgent warning.
normal_cases: Acknowledge an equipment caution: its attention cue resets under the adopted policy while the physical fault and specific indication remain.
limit_cases: An urgent noncancellable warning cannot be dismissed by ordinary caution acknowledgement.
failure_recovery_cases: Repair clears the physical condition; a later recurrence creates a fresh attention event.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: A second fault can demand attention while an acknowledged fault persists
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: Pass stable cause IDs and occurrence counters into attention arbitration. Acknowledge the occurrences actually presented, retain active acknowledged faults, and re-alert on a newly qualifying cause without demanding that every previous cause first disappear.
normal_cases: Fault A produces attention; acknowledge A; adding B produces a new adopted attention event while A remains active.
limit_cases: Repeated samples of unchanged A do not masquerade as new occurrences; A+B resolved/recurred have intentional rules.
failure_recovery_cases: Source invalidity, power loss and mission reset do not revive old acknowledgements or erase a genuine new occurrence.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Urgent audio response has a latency budget across an occupied voice slot
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: Declare and measure end-to-end visual/aural onset budgets for each adopted alert family, including occupied slots and native audio. Preserve intelligibility; add preemption only where the chosen urgency policy requires it. Do not claim an exact F-22 audio scheduler.
normal_cases: Low-priority voice followed by an urgent alert has recorded onset, completion and priority transitions.
limit_cases: Repeated direction changes and simultaneous RWR/MWS/terrain events do not create overlapping unintelligible speech or indefinitely postpone an urgent cue.
failure_recovery_cases: Failed/sticky/frozen sound status releases its bounded lease and current conditions are reconsidered rather than replaying an obsolete queue.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Global voice inhibit and retained-mute awareness are separate choices
findings.applicability: Global mute has a named DCS Viper analogue. General civil alert-design guidance is optional; actual F-22 mute controls, minimum volume and retained-state indications are unknown.
findings.change: Choose the voice-inhibit/volume policy explicitly. Global voice inhibit is a documented Viper-like option and should not be called an F-22 defect merely because it suppresses urgent speech. Retained suppression awareness, rearm controls and any separation of critical/nonessential audio are optional design decisions; exact F-22 controls remain unresolved.
normal_cases: Mute own voice on AUDIO, leave that page and retain recognizable adopted suppression state.
limit_cases: Zero volume and mute are both handled intentionally; acknowledgement does not silently become permanent suppression.
failure_recovery_cases: Power/slot/mission restoration has a declared mute persistence policy and cannot leave an unannunciated retained mute.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: A voice playback test does not verify annunciators or equipment sensing
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: Keep VOICE TEST scoped to audio. Add an adopted annunciator test and equipment-specific test paths only for declared modeled equipment. State which power/source failures each test can detect; test presentation must not create actual fire, damage or automatic repair.
normal_cases: Exercise audio and annunciator paths separately with their required sources powered.
limit_cases: An actual urgent condition during test has the adopted priority and truthful indication; the test cannot acknowledge it.
failure_recovery_cases: Missing sound/annunciator or equipment source is reported as the appropriate test limitation, not an equipment-all-clear.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: A fault-specific checklist link is separate from a static phase checklist
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: If adopted, connect stable modeled fault IDs to the appropriate supported reference checklist and allow deliberate pilot selection among simultaneous faults. Use validated procedures for the chosen simulation; do not auto-complete unobservable steps or infer unpublished emergency procedures.
normal_cases: Selecting a supported active fault opens its matching approved simulation reference.
limit_cases: Multiple faults and unavailable procedure data remain distinguishable; no generic cold-start list is mislabeled as the response.
failure_recovery_cases: Acknowledgement, display relocation or one-page failure does not lose the fault-to-reference association.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Multiple active conditions retain identity when one alert wins attention
findings.applicability: The real F-22 interaction schedule is not established. The named comparator supplies a proposed simulation policy, not a mandatory recovered F-22 procedure.
findings.change: If adopting an integrated list, retain each active condition and occurrence independently of the top attention cue. Make hidden-active state/overflow/recall explicit, and keep active conditions separate from maintenance history. Exact F-22 capacity and key actions remain unresolved.
normal_cases: Two supported conditions retain their identities while the higher-priority one drives immediate attention.
limit_cases: A full display gives honest hidden-active information; clearing a view does not clear a physical condition.
failure_recovery_cases: Condition recovery, source invalidity and new occurrence update the list with distinct meanings.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Cleared bleed overtemperature does not imply restored oxygen/cooling supply
findings.applicability: Historical 2010 equipped-aircraft event/function evidence. No endorsement of accident causation, physiological timing or unchanged current-fleet software. No operational emergency procedure is inferred.
findings.change: For a compatible dated profile, separate leak/temperature detection, automatic protective isolation, available bleed/conditioned supply and each dependent alert. Clearing hot temperature must not silently reopen the isolated source or declare oxygen/cooling restored. Keep modern backup equipment, exact timing and thresholds explicit rather than cloning a mishap timeline.
normal_cases: A synthetic modeled leak triggers the declared protective isolation and truthful supply/alert states.
limit_cases: Temperature normalizes after isolation: the hot indication can clear while downstream unavailable conditions remain.
failure_recovery_cases: Supply is restored only by the supported declared recovery path; backup oxygen status remains independent.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Probe heating controls and sensor validity are distinct from true icing aerodynamics
findings.applicability: DCS control-workflow comparison plus general weather physics; total host weather response unresolved.
findings.change: Choose an explicitly estimated probe-protection/sensor-failure profile and identify host ownership first. Keep sensed pressure/validity separate from true aerodynamic airflow, and keep airframe/inlet icing effects distinct from probe failure. Adopt qualitative physics without importing another aircraft’s accretion rates or switch labels.
normal_cases: Compare declared heater OFF/ON/AUTO and test/fault status with electrical and airborne conditions.
limit_cases: Compare cold dry air, visible moisture and a warm condition without equating low temperature alone with accretion.
failure_recovery_cases: Block/fail a sensed probe while retaining true aerodynamic state; restore heating/sensing according to a declared estimate.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Defog airflow and exterior rain removal are different physical functions
findings.applicability: Historical F-22 function with later schematic corroboration; modern detailed controls/limits unresolved.
findings.change: Represent an applicable defog airflow/control dependency and identify the host visibility interface before adding graphics. Keep internal fog, external precipitation and thermal/anti-ice behavior separate. Use labeled humidity/clearing estimates; do not copy Hornet air temperatures or pretend a tint change clears condensation.
normal_cases: Use the declared defog control at an appropriate powered ECS condition and observe actual visibility or supported host clearing effect.
limit_cases: Compare an internally fogged condition with exterior rain and a dry canopy; use distinct states.
failure_recovery_cases: Remove/recover conditioned air and retain moisture/thermal lag rather than clearing the canopy instantly through a cosmetic setting.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Canopy position, hold and secondary lock are separate states
findings.applicability: Historical F-22 mechanical/function description; native simulator behavior unresolved.
findings.change: Establish inherited UP/STOP/DOWN and lock/power behavior, then add only missing supported states. Keep selected lock, achieved closure and cabin sealing distinct. A simplified ground manual recovery can be declared without reproducing rescue tooling or historical software-handshake defects.
normal_cases: Open, stop at an intermediate height, close and distinguish achieved position from selected/latched lock.
limit_cases: Compare powered and declared no-power paths; a closed drawing alone must not prove sealing/locking.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose power during movement, select/release lock and recover according to one explicit state contract.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Cabin differential pressure is a separate exported physical state
findings.applicability: Owned physical export and public system function; exact F-22 curve and host pilot effects unqualified.
findings.change: Provide a bounded differential-pressure state tied to declared source, achieved sealing and vent/leak availability, and publish it through the documented interface. Keep normal schedules, leak/decompression rates and controls estimated unless sourced. Reconcile indication with the same pressure state and keep breathing-gas pressure separate.
normal_cases: With a declared sealed/pressurized configuration, compare ambient, cabin increment and the resulting indication at several altitudes.
limit_cases: Compare source off, ventilation/dump and a declared leak independently of oxygen product pressure.
failure_recovery_cases: Lose/recover sealing or pressure source with finite state response; do not restore pressure merely by clearing a warning.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Cold-soaked auxiliary-power readiness is not established by ambient engine indication
findings.applicability: Historical logistics evidence, not a current flight-manual limit.
findings.change: Record the historical ground-support dependency and decide whether cold-soak readiness is within the chosen mod profile. If adopted, use explicit estimated soak/preheat state and supported ground service, retaining residual warmth. Obtain operating-envelope evidence before claiming an authentic threshold or mandatory wait.
normal_cases: Compare a sheltered/warm and a declared cold-soaked ground state under the adopted abstraction.
limit_cases: Separate ambient temperature, soak duration and residual warmth; do not assume the source supplies their boundaries.
failure_recovery_cases: Abort/retry after preheat or partial warm-up without resetting all thermal state or inventing source energy.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: A healthy pressure indication need not equal geometric altitude in nonstandard temperature
findings.applicability: General physical/instrument behavior only. Civil CTA operating requirements are not imported as military rules, and no automatic F-22 compensation is assumed.
findings.change: Keep weather-related indication error distinct from sensor/data invalidity and from optional corrected guidance.
normal_cases: For a declared nonstandard atmosphere, compare pressure-derived indication and true geometry without forcing equality.
limit_cases: A healthy nonstandard-temperature indication remains distinguishable from stale/nonfinite pressure; resetting QNH is not a generic temperature-correction command.
failure_recovery_cases: Actual pressure/source failure triggers its validity policy without erasing the separately available geometric clearance used by other systems.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Healthy barometric altitude is coupled to unrelated CAS computation in the HUD
findings.applicability: Selected generic/analogue partial-data behavior. Actual physical failure generation, integrated-ADC failover and Raptor display policy require separate evidence.
findings.change: Separate healthy pressure-altitude presentation from the CAS-computation success branch.
normal_cases: With fresh baro and valid flight-path data, invalidate only the TAS/CAS input and retain the chosen healthy baro display.
limit_cases: When a declared common static/ADC failure invalidates both source families, inhibit both explicitly; keep independent UFD/HUD source semantics consistent.
failure_recovery_cases: Restore the individual input and recover only its affected presentation without stale-value jumps or spurious source changes.
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.

findings.behavior: Ownship identification replies are a separate function from interrogating other contacts
findings.applicability: The ownship identification role is a dated direct F-22 requirement. Exact modes, codes, timing and UI are proposed substitutes. DCS Viper itself does not fully implement code editing, so its guide is not proof of complete cryptographic fidelity.
findings.change: Model ownship identification separately from contact interrogation, using a declared abstract game contract and truthful host capability limits.
normal_cases: With transponder enabled, a qualified incoming game interrogation yields the declared reply/indication; SCAN/LOS actions still query other contacts independently.
Radar off with surviving CNI power preserves the independently supported responder role under the adopted supply policy.
limit_cases: Absent or incompatible abstract identification credentials do not produce an authenticated friendly reply. No real encryption or protocol is modeled.
Own PPLI availability alone is not shown as proof that a separate transponder replied.
failure_recovery_cases: Loss/recovery of CNI supply or the selected resource fault shows unavailable/recovered identification state without silently inheriting interrogation consent.
Emergency identification, if offered, has an explicit pilot-selected state and clear reset behavior.
findings.requirement_kind: Adopt dated F-22 ownship identification role; propose abstract controls and host-limited mechanism
findings.status: Audit proposal or retention criteria; no aircraft implementation changed
findings.audit_action: Proposal/retention criteria only; no aircraft implementation changed by analysis.
